Meeting Date:  June 3, 2025
From:  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
Department:  City Administration
Submitted by:  Angela Kimmey, Deputy City Administrator

Subject
Vernon Reads! Summer Reading Program

Recommendation
Approve the Vernon Reads! Summer Reading Program, consisting of the Summer Reading
Bingo Challenge, the Escape into Reading Summer Book Reviews, and prizes for participation.

Background
In the absence of traditional brick-and-mortar City-operated libraries, City staff sought creative
solutions to encourage literacy, make books available to the community, and inspire a love of
reading and learning. Research suggests that American children are reading for leisure at a
declining rate compared to children in prior decades. Research also indicates that reading for
pleasure is becoming less popular amongst adults, and those who still read for pleasure are
reading less per day. The Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program, approved by the Library Board
of Trustees at its Special Meeting on November 5, 2024, encourages reading as a lifelong skill
that improves memory, builds a robust vocabulary, builds a foundation of knowledge, and
provides significant physical and mental health benefits for Vernon residents and children.

In further support of these goals, it is proposed that the Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program
include a Summer Reading Program to encourage kids and teens to take time during the summer
to incorporate reading for fun. City staff met with the Library Board of Trustees Ad Hoc Committee
members to review and discuss the proposed summer reading program, supplemental program
elements, and prizes for participation. The Ad Hoc Committee recommends the Summer Reading
Program for the Library Board of Trustees' consideration.

The Summer Reading Program will also support and encourage families who have received
Amazon Kindle E-book readers with Kids+ e-book subscriptions from the Vernon Reads! Virtual
Library Program to use their E-book readers to participate. The Summer Reading Program will
include two elements:

  1) A traditional summer reading log branded as the Vernon Reads! Escape into Reading
  Summer Book Reviews where participants list books that have been read and write mini
  book reviews; and
  2) A Summer Reading Bingo Challenge where participants complete various reading-related
  tasks noted on a bingo card.

While reading for fun is its own reward, the Vernon Reads! Summer Reading Program will include
prizes for participation. Participants who submit four mini book reviews or complete five reading
activities in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) to achieve “bingo” will receive two free
books of their choosing from the City’s collection for their home libraries. Participants will also be
entered into a raffle to win one of three annual Bookroo monthly book club subscriptions for kids

  Item 2  Page 7 of 14
 and one of several gift card prizes. Bookroo subscriptions include a monthly delivery of two hard
cover books, by age group. Any participant who completes all reading activities noted on the
bingo sheet or submits 10 book reviews will be entered into the Grand Prize Raffle to win a laptop
computer.

The Bookroo Book Club subscriptions, gift cards, and grand prize laptop computer will be
purchased using existing Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program budgeted funds. The raffles will
take place at the City's National Night Out event on August 5, 2025. Participants do not need to
be present to win but must submit their bingo worksheets or book reviews electronically via text
or email prior to the August 5th deadline in order to be eligible for raffle prize entry. The Summer
Reading Program will be promoted via social media and will be advertised on the City’s website
and directly with Vernon residents and the Vernon City Elementary School.

The Summer Reading Program Bingo Challenge and Escape into Reading Summer Book
Reviews support the Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program’s stated goals of encouraging
literacy, making books available to the community, and inspiring a love of reading and learning.
All Summer Reading Program prizes encourage learning, increase access to books, and support
the development of home libraries.

Fiscal Impact
The fiscal impact is estimated at $2,000. Sufficient funds are available in General Fund,
Community Development, Good Neighbor Program, Account No. 011-010-160-529715 for the
current fiscal year.
